findings.title: Date override short-circuits busy checks
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, once any date override is deemed to fall on the slot's calendar day and the slot is not rejected as outside that window, the function returns true immediately. That return happens before the busy-interval loop, so bookings, calendar busy times, and buffers passed in as busy are ignored for every slot on a day that has a date override. Fixed-host and round-robin filtering both call this helper with the host's busy list, so a host can be offered (and booked) during an override window where they already have a conflict.

findings.title: Any non-covering override rejects the slot
findings.body: dateOverrides.find treats a callback return of true as "slot is unavailable". The callback returns true when the slot ends at or before that override's start or starts after that override's end. If a host has more than one override window on the same day (for example 09:00-10:00 and 14:00-16:00), the window that does not contain the slot makes find succeed and the function returns false, even when another window fully contains the slot. Multiple date overrides on one day, which the product supports, will hide valid slots.

findings.title: All-day block override is never detected
findings.body: The unavailable-all-day case is written as dayjs(start).add(offset) === dayjs(end).add(offset). Dayjs instances are never strictly equal, so this branch never runs. A date override stored with equal start and end (the usual "block this day" shape) therefore does not force the slot unavailable. Combined with the later dateOverrideExist return, that day can be treated as open instead of blocked.

findings.title: Working-hours gate does not enforce the host's day
findings.body: The new working-hours check only returns false when it finds a WorkingHours row whose days include slotStartTime.day() and whose range excludes the slot. If the fixed host has no row for that weekday, find returns nothing and the slot is treated as inside working hours. Also both start and end minutes are computed from slotStartTime, so a slot that starts inside the range and ends past workingHour.endTime is not rejected. Round-robin aggregate slots that exist because another host works that day still pass for a fixed host who does not.

findings.title: Override day compare mixes local and UTC formatting
findings.body: The override side is dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset).format("YYYY MM DD"), which formats in the process local timezone, while slotStartTime is time.utc() and formats in UTC. On any server whose local zone is not UTC, the same instant can format as different calendar days, so a fixed host's override is applied to the wrong day or not applied at all. Availability then depends on where the Node process is running.

findings.title: Timezone offset wraps override times at midnight
findings.body: Override start and end are shifted by inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset and then reduced with .hour() and .minute() only. Those accessors wrap at 00:00/24:00, so a negative or positive offset that crosses midnight turns an evening window into a morning minute-of-day (or the reverse) on the invitee's current day instead of the adjacent day. Large timezone gaps, which this change is meant to fix, still produce the wrong slots or drop the override.

findings.title: New tests do not cover the stated fixes
findings.body: The added assertion only re-queries a single-user event in Asia/Dhaka and expects the same UTC slot list as the IST case. It does not cover a round-robin event with a fixed host date override (the #8207 fix), a blocked day, multiple override windows, a busy time inside an override, or a timezone offset large enough to cross midnight. Those are exactly the paths the new checkIfIsAvailable and offset math get wrong, so this suite will stay green while those bookings are still incorrect.
